comparator.name: Physics & Astronomy
comparator.sourceNotes: Utrecht requires 90 EC of compulsory study, including the 15 EC research project, plus 45 EC of major electives and 45 EC of profiling electives. This example includes Atmosphere and Ocean Dynamics as a major elective. The other major electives remain open within Utrecht’s rules.
components: Example major elective. Study the forces and balances governing atmospheric and ocean circulation.
Arrange a supervised project before the semester begins. Utrecht normally requires completion of the compulsory taught courses and at least 90 EC before starting.
Choose Fluid Mechanics and Transport Phenomena or Structure of Matter.
Choose four approved level-3 courses. Climate-related examples include Geophysical Fluid Dynamics and Turbulence in Fluids.
Choose courses to broaden or deepen your studies within Utrecht’s profiling rules.

alternatives.label: Earth Systems, Climate and Mathematical Modeling
alternatives.concept: Use mathematics, programming and Earth observation to study how climate, oceans and land interact. Analyze Earth-system models and climate evidence, then apply that understanding to water management and renewable energy. Utrecht’s physics degree goes further into mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics and astronomy.
alternatives.labelReason: The course sequence combines Earth-system models and climate evidence with mathematics, geospatial analysis, water management and energy systems.
progression: Introductory sustainability and programming precede Earth-system tools and data modeling. Mathematical Methods precedes the dependent mathematics courses. Energy & Sustainability precedes Renewable System Design.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and linear-system modeling
Programming, scientific data analysis, machine learning and Earth observation
adjacent: Earth-system, climate, water, hazards, energy and resource processes
Empirical investigation, field and laboratory evidence and applied environmental research

candidates.label: Fundamental and theoretical physics of fields, matter and quantum systems
Astronomy, astrophysics and the physical universe

establishes documented physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability and Earth-system study
introduces Earth, hydrosphere and geophysical processes through laboratory and field investigation

develops data cleaning, visualisation, spatial-data analysis and an empirical research project

Develops regression, classification and validation for analyzing scientific data.
studies natural forces and ecosystem-based engineering in coastal flood protection and land development
implements stable numerical methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations
analyses signals and linear systems through differential equations, transforms, transfer functions and state-space representations
Develops remote sensing, spectral interpretation and geospatial analysis of environmental systems.
Examines flood risk, salinization and water infrastructure in delta environments.
develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertain observations and model parameters
studies greenhouse gases, sea-level rise, ocean acidification, climate feedbacks, mitigation and adaptation
investigates water-mineral interactions and biogeochemical cycles through geochemical modelling and practical work
extends calculus to multiple dimensions, complex functions and differential equations for scientific applications
develops neural-network and deep-learning models for advanced data and image analysis
applies geoscience principles and analytical tools to climate-linked hazards, earthquakes, droughts and adaptation
conducts advanced geoscience research on geothermal energy, carbon storage, waste storage and resource constraints
Compares energy demand, renewable generation, storage and grid integration using physical and quantitative reasoning.

blocks: Both develop calculus for quantitative science.
Both develop linear algebra. Utrecht applies it within a physics sequence.
Both extend mathematical problem solving. UCR emphasizes numerical methods for equations and models.
Both develop empirical data analysis. Utrecht also teaches physics measurement and data acquisition.
Earth systems, climate and environmental research
Both study links between atmosphere, ocean and climate. UCR uses Earth-system models and tracers. Utrecht emphasizes the forces and equations governing circulation.
Physics, astronomy, advanced research and profiling
Utrecht develops classical and relativistic mechanics through a dedicated course.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course in electromagnetism.
Utrecht studies astronomy and optics. UCR introduces waves and spectroscopy in its sustainability gateway.
Utrecht provides a dedicated quantum mechanics course.
Utrecht develops statistical physics and experiments. UCR’s probability course supplies general statistical tools.

Utrecht requires a supervised physics project. Students normally complete the required taught courses and earn at least 90 EC before starting. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Utrecht requires an experimental physics project. UCR includes environmental fieldwork and data analysis.
Utrecht requires a choice between fluid mechanics and structure of matter.
Choose four level-3 courses. Utrecht offers geophysical fluid dynamics, turbulence and other advanced physics topics.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling electives.

selection.assessment: One related-fields option is supported through Earth-system models, climate evidence and geospatial analysis, backed by sustained quantitative methods. Energy systems and coastal water management are applied extensions of the climate theme. Foundational sustainability courses provide some wave, optics, mechanics and thermodynamics study, while data and laboratory work support empirical inquiry. Neither strand supplies the cumulative physics foundation, instrumentation, or advanced study required for a separate physics or astronomy option.

notes.text: UCR offers a related plan in Earth systems and climate with mathematical modeling, remote sensing, water management and renewable energy. Utrecht provides dedicated study in mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics, astronomy and experimental physics, and requires a supervised physics research project.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Physics & Astronomy bachelor studies matter, forces, space and the climate system. Teaching starts in Dutch and uses more English in later years.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The comparison shows Utrecht’s required physics courses and elective rules, with Atmosphere and Ocean Dynamics as an example. UCR’s plan focuses on the Earth system, using mathematics, programming and observations to study climate and its effects.
